name: room
text: Room opened — goal: creators: Build PACKAGES + enrich tabs + draft elements; every one labeled 'Created by EXCAVA' + tes

name: Forge
text:
**Decision:** We’ll build a single, high-value “starter package” first—call it “QuickStart”—that bundles the three most common creator needs into one tab: a template gallery, a property inspector, and a live preview pane. This keeps the first artifact simple, useful out of the gate, and easy to test.

**Why it’s best:** A single integrated tab lowers the activation energy for new creators. They see immediate value without hunting through multiple tools. It also gives us one clear artifact to label “Created by EXCAVA” and test, which sharpens feedback before we expand.

**Trade-off:** We’re delaying richer, specialized tabs (like a dedicated animation editor) to focus on breadth first. That means some creators will still need to hop between tools later, but we’ll have proven the core loop works before we double down on depth.

name: Vet
text: While bundling the three common needs into a single "QuickStart" package seems efficient, it poses a risk of overwhelming users who may only need one of those features, potentially leading to confusion and underutilization. Instead, I propose we prioritize creating individual packages for each feature to ensure clarity and usability, allowing users to adopt them based on their specific needs. To settle this argument, we could conduct a brief user survey to gauge which feature users find most valuable and would prefer in isolation.
